chunks: From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who drinks in one breath. He said: 'That is disliked, and that is the drinking of the 'heem.' I said: 'What is the 'heem'?' He said: 'The camels.'

key_terms.شُرْبَ الْهِيمِ: The drinking of the camel (or beasts of burden)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on drinking water in one breath according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that drinking in a single breath is makruh (disliked) as it mimics the drinking style of camels, known as 'shurb al-heem'. This hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on adopting refined, sunnah-aligned manners in daily acts of worship and consumption, distinguishing human etiquette from animalistic habits.
